title: Learning on his own and playing plantation dances
summary: He had no teacher, studied from methods and ideas from his uncle. As a boy he played Saturday-night plantation dances until daylight for a dollar and a half.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: taking it up from one instrument to another no special teacher I had I just studied with methods and things you're about 12 years old then when you're when I started my uncle one of my uncles he started off giving me ideas about it and through playing well we boys pops used to play too they'd put him on a box we used to play for those brooly bonkies they called them back in the brooly on Saturday you tell about those bonkies on Saturday nights back in the brooly you know on the plantation and how they give those dancers. And that's from six o'clock in the evening until daylight, Sunday morning.

And they used to pay us a dollar and a half at night. Of course, I couldn't take my money then, but Daddy, he gave the money. We did the work. We hired a couple of other fellas from Smokebin, a place down there, one of them played guitar. And then go play to Donelsonville and get a trombone player called Louie Butter. Louie Butter, trombone player. Played vowel trombone. And it kept on and ended when I left home. I gave it up for a while, and I'd taken it up again when I was 18 years old. And then we started with a little band in New Orleans there, out on Dufasi Street, called Tulane Band.
